transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I, um, I hope I’m in the right place for this. It's probably nothing major, just a little quirk, really... but, well, what brings me in is that sometimes people at the museum will be talking right to me, maybe about the next art walk or something. And I’ll be looking right at them, but then I realize I completely missed the middle of what they said. 

I end up having to ask them to run it by me again. I always feel a bit foolish when it happens, and I really don't want them to think I'm being rude or ignoring them. It’s just a minor thing, I'm sure, and I hate to take up your time with it, but... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you help with?
When you realize you've missed part of what someone was saying, do you think it's because you weren't paying attention or because you just couldn't make sense of what they were saying?

Oh, gosh... that's a really good question. Um... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. 

I don't think it's that I can't make sense of it. The words make perfect sense, I just... well, maybe my mind just wanders a tiny bit? Just for a split second. I really try to be a good listener, I promise I'm not doing it on purpose to be disrespectful or anything. I always want to be polite to the folks at the museum. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm sorry, I wish I could give you a clearer answer... is it okay if I'm not a hundred percent sure about that?
When your mind wanders for that split second, are you usually thinking about something else or is it more like a blank space?

Well, um... I guess it's a bit of both? Sometimes I might just be thinking about, oh, I don't know, whether I remembered to lock the front door, or if I need to pick up milk on the way home. Just silly, everyday things, you know? 

But other times, it's... it's just sort of a little pause. Like a blank space, I suppose. It's not that I'm ignoring them, I promise. It's just a tiny little blip. I hope that's a normal thing to happen sometimes? I really try my best to stay focused on the person in front of me. Am I explaining that alright?
Do these little blips or mind wanderings cause you any distress or problems in your daily life?

Well, I... I wouldn't say it's a huge problem, really. I mean, I'm retired, so it's not like I'm messing up at a big corporate job or anything. It's mostly just... well, at the museum. 

I volunteer there a lot, and... I guess the group has had to, um, quietly shift some of the planning pieces away from me lately. Just the little organizational things. They're all so sweet about it, they really are, they just say they want to take some things off my plate. But I know it's because I keep missing details. 

And, um... I've actually stopped leading the art walks the way I used to. I just... I stopped feeling as confident doing it, I suppose. I didn't want to let anyone down if I lost my train of thought while I was talking to the visitors. 

It's really not a tragedy or anything, I still love being there! I just... I hope it doesn't make me sound incompetent. I really do try to be helpful to them. Does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you ever find yourself forgetting things that happened recently, like what you did yesterday or what you were supposed to do today?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I have any trouble like that. My memory for what happened yesterday or, you know, what I need to do today is perfectly fine. 

I mean, everyone misplaces their keys once in a blue moon, right? But I definitely know what I did yesterday, and I always know what my schedule is. I'm very careful about that sort of thing. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm losing my marbles or anything like that! 

I really try to keep my days organized. Is it okay that I don't have that problem? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you find yourself having trouble focusing or following along in other situations, like when watching TV, reading a book, or having conversations with friends and family?

Well, um... I guess with reading, sometimes it can be a little tricky. Not that I can't read, of course! I love reading. But, well, for example, if I sit down with a new gallery packet at the museum, or even just some notes I need to review... I'll start out just fine. I really do try to pay attention. 

But then, after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes are still moving over the words, but my mind has just... wandered off somewhere else entirely. And then I have to go back and read the same part all over again. It's a bit silly, really. I always get it done eventually, I just have to reread things a few times. 

It's not a terrible problem, is it? I mean, I'm sure lots of people get a little distracted when they read, right? I just want to make sure I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill. Am I giving you the right kind of information?
Do you ever feel mentally foggy or confused, even if it's just for a brief moment?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't get confused or foggy, really. I mean, my mind might wander off to what I'm making for dinner while I'm trying to read something, but I always know where I am and what's going on. 

I'm definitely not walking around in a daze or anything like that! I like to think I'm still pretty sharp for my age, you know? Just a little easily sidetracked sometimes. That's a different thing than being confused, isn't it? I hope I'm explaining that right. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my faculties or anything!
Are there other areas of your life, outside of the museum, where you feel like your mind wandering or missing details is causing problems?

Well, um... I suppose... I mean, I really don't want it to sound like I'm incapable or anything. I'm still very involved! But, well, I guess at the museum... some of the other volunteers have, very kindly, taken over some of the planning pieces I used to handle. Just quietly, you know? They're so sweet about it. 

And, um, to be perfectly honest... I haven't been doing the art walks as much lately. I just... I don't feel quite as confident leading them the way I used to, in case I lose my train of thought or miss a detail about one of the paintings. I wouldn't want to give the visitors the wrong impression of the museum. 

But I'm still helping out in other ways! I'm still a good volunteer, I promise. It's just a small adjustment, really. That's not too terrible, is it? I hope it's okay that I stepped back a little bit.
Have you noticed any changes in how your friends and family interact with you since you started experiencing these mind wanderings?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, my family and friends are just wonderful. They haven't said anything at all. 

I suppose... well, maybe my wife will gently remind me if I've forgotten to take out the recycling, or if I lose track of a story she's telling me. But she's never upset about it! She just sort of chuckles and repeats herself. It's nothing that causes any real trouble or arguments. 

Everyone is very patient with me. I really try my best to be present when I'm with them. I'm sure it's just normal getting-older stuff, right? I certainly hope I'm not being a burden to anyone. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of things.
Do you find yourself zoning out or losing focus when you're doing things like cooking, gardening, or other activities that take a while to complete?

Well, um... with things like cooking or working in the yard, I usually do alright. I think keeping my hands busy helps. But... I suppose I do notice something a bit like that when I'm trying to read. 

Like, if I sit down with a new gallery packet or a set of notes for the museum, I always start out just fine! I really do try to pay attention. But then, after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes are still moving over the page, but my mind has just... wandered off somewhere else entirely. And then I have to go back and read the exact same part all over again. 

It's nothing too terrible, I promise! Just a little silly of me. I'm sure that happens to almost everyone when they're reading, doesn't it? Especially if the material is a little dry. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples. I hope that's the sort of thing you were asking about?
Are there any other areas of your daily life, outside of volunteering and the museum, where you feel like your mind wandering is causing problems?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, my day-to-day life is pretty quiet now that I'm not working. I just putter around the house, maybe watch a little television or run some simple errands... there's not really much else that demands a lot of strict attention, you know? 

So I wouldn't say it's causing any actual problems anywhere else. I manage quite well at home, I promise! I just... I really don't want you to think I'm completely disorganized or falling apart. Everything else is perfectly fine. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have any more examples for you? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly and giving you what you need.
Do you find it harder to learn new things now than you used to?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's harder, exactly. I mean, I'm 63 now, so I don't expect my brain to work exactly like it did when I was in my twenties, you know? 

I still enjoy learning things! I really do. If it's something I'm interested in, I feel like I pick it up just fine. Maybe I have to read a set of instructions twice instead of once, but I always get there in the end. I don't feel like I've lost a step or anything like that. 

I think that's pretty normal for someone my age, isn't it? Just taking a little extra time to absorb things? I certainly don't feel like I'm struggling with it. I hope that answers what you were asking... I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of how I'm doing.
Have you noticed any changes in how your wife interacts with you when you lose your train of thought or miss details in conversations with her?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say there's been any real changes with her. My wife is a wonderful woman, very patient. I mean, sure, sometimes I might miss a little detail if she's telling me about her day while I'm trying to fix something in the kitchen, but she knows I don't mean anything by it. 

If I lose my train of thought, she might just gently remind me what we were talking about. It's never a big deal, I promise! We don't argue about it or anything like that. I think after being married this long, you just get used to each other's little quirks, don't you? 

I really don't want you to think it's causing problems in my marriage. We get along beautifully. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need without making things sound worse than they are.
Do you feel like your mind wandering or missing details has changed how your friends and family view you or interact with you?

Oh, um... no, I really haven't noticed anything like that. My friends and my kids, they treat me exactly the same as they always have. 

I mean, sure, maybe they'll tease me a little bit if I forget why I walked into a room or if I zone out during a long story, but it's all in good fun, you know? They certainly don't look at me differently or treat me like I'm... well, incapable or anything. I really wouldn't want you to get the impression that my relationships are suffering, because they really aren't. Everyone is just wonderful to me. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a big dramatic example for you there? I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so I'm doing this right for you.
Are there any daily activities outside of the museum where you feel your mind wandering is causing you difficulties?

Well, um... not really, no. I mean, I do my daily chores, I run errands, I putter around the house... and I manage all of that just fine. 

I suppose sometimes I might go to the grocery store for milk and come back with three other things and forget the milk, but... well, who hasn't done that, right? It's just a little scatterbrained moment, nothing that really causes any real trouble. I just make another trip, or we have toast instead of cereal. It's not a big deal at all.

I really don't feel like I'm struggling with my day-to-day life. I keep the house tidy, I pay the bills... I might have to double-check my math on the checkbook sometimes if my mind drifts, but I always catch it. I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for? I just want to reassure you that I'm managing everything okay.
Do you feel like your mind wandering or missing details is significantly impacting your overall quality of life?

Well, um... I wouldn't say *significantly*, no. My life is very good, really. I'm very lucky. 

I mean... I suppose there is one little thing, but it's not a huge deal. At the museum where I volunteer... well, the group has had to quietly shift a few of the planning pieces away from me lately. Just little administrative things. And... well, I guess I've stopped feeling quite as confident leading the art walks the way I used to. I just worry I might lose my place in the history spiel, you know? 

But honestly, it's fine! It just means I get to help out in other ways, like greeting people at the door. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or that my life is falling apart, because it absolutely isn't. I'm still very happy to be there. I hope it's okay that I mentioned that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details, even the silly ones.
Do you find your mind wandering when you're in the middle of a task that requires you to focus for a longer period?

Well, um... I guess it depends on what you mean by a longer period, really. I mean, I can certainly focus when I need to! 

But, well, if I sit down with, say, a gallery packet or a new set of notes for the museum... I usually start out just fine. I'm very interested in the material, of course. But then, after a few minutes, I might realize that my eyes are still moving over the page, but my mind has just sort of... wandered off somewhere else entirely. And then I have to go back and read the same part all over again. 

It's just a little quirk, really. I always get through the reading eventually, I promise! It just might take me a tiny bit longer than it used to. I hope that's the sort of example you were looking for? I'm doing my best to give you good answers.
Have you noticed any changes in how your family interacts with you when you're not volunteering at the museum?

Well, um... no, not really. My family is wonderful, they really are. We all get along just beautifully. 

I mean, my wife and kids... they're always so supportive and kind. I haven't noticed any big changes or anything like that. We still have our lovely Sunday dinners, and I still help out with the grandkids when they need me. Everything at home is just... well, it's just fine, really. 

I hope that's okay to say? I don't want it to sound like I'm hiding anything, I just... I really haven't noticed any differences in how they treat me. We're a very close-knit bunch, you see. Is that the kind of thing you were wondering about?
Have you experienced any physical symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness in your body?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that at all. Physically, I'm really doing quite well, thank you for asking. 

I mean, maybe I get a little stiff in the knees now and then, but just the normal things for someone my age, you know? Definitely no numbness or tingling or weakness or anything scary like that. I'm very lucky that way. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have anything to report for that one? I know you have to ask all these questions to do your job properly and get the whole picture, so I just want to make sure I'm still giving you exactly what you need. Is that an okay answer?
Do you think your mind wandering has affected how your wife interacts with you?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. My wife is just the most patient woman in the world, she really is. 

I mean, sometimes if she's talking to me and I'm a little... distracted, maybe thinking about a new exhibit or something, she might have to repeat herself. But she never gets upset! She just sort of chuckles and taps my arm and says, "Earth to dear," and we both have a little laugh about it. It's really not a problem at all, just a tiny little quirk of mine. 

She's always so wonderful about everything. I certainly don't think it's caused any sort of trouble between us. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how things are at home. I'm doing okay with these questions, aren't I?
